segments.t: Sofia arrives to audition for a film role. The casting director wants the choreography first and the acting scene afterwards, but Sofia begins with an improvised action performance. Listen first in French.
Sofia, on y va?
Oui, je suis prête.
Je m'appelle Sofia Leprince, j'ai 25 ans.
Et mon agent est Gabriel Sarda chez ASK.
Parfait! On commence tout de suite.
D'abord la chorégraphie, ensuite votre scène, d'accord?
D'accord, quand vous voulez.
Ils veulent se battre avec moi?
Je cours plus vite qu'eux!
Maintenant je suis là, maintenant je ne suis plus là!
Vous me voyez atterrir comme une héroïne?
Ce n'est pas du tout ce que j'avais demandé.
Now let's walk through the audition scene line by line and examine the key French phrases.
Sofia, on y va?
'Sofia, shall we go?' The two short words after 'we' express going there or getting started. With rising intonation, this becomes 'shall we begin?'.
Oui, je suis prête.
'Yes, I am ready.' The last word means ready. Its feminine written ending matches Sofia, who is saying she is ready to begin the audition.
Je m'appelle Sofia Leprince, j'ai 25 ans.
'My name is Sofia Leprince, I am twenty-five years old.' The first action literally says 'I call myself', the everyday way to give a name. Age then uses 'have', followed by a number of years.
Et mon agent est Gabriel Sarda chez ASK.
'And my agent is Gabriel Sarda at ASK.' The small word before the agency's name means 'at' or 'with'. It identifies where her agent works rather than where Sofia is standing.
Parfait! On commence tout de suite.
'Perfect! We start right away.' The first word means perfect. The final three-word expression means 'immediately' or 'right away', so the start will not be delayed.
D'abord la chorégraphie, ensuite votre scène, d'accord?
'First the choreography, then your scene, okay?' Two ordering words organize the tasks: first choreography, then the acting scene. The final check asks whether Sofia agrees to that order.
D'accord, quand vous voulez.
'Okay, whenever you want.' The opening accepts the instruction. The remaining words literally mean 'when you want', inviting the casting director to choose when to start.
Ils veulent se battre avec moi?
'They want to fight with me?' The words after 'want' mean fighting one another. The final 'with me' identifies Sofia's character as the person they want to confront.
Je cours plus vite qu'eux!
'I run faster than them!' The comparison joins 'more' and 'fast' to make 'faster'. The shortened word before 'them' means 'than', identifying the people she outruns.
Maintenant je suis là, maintenant je ne suis plus là!
'Now I am here, now I am no longer here!' The word for 'now' is repeated in both halves. The second half adds a negative meaning 'no longer', so she acts out disappearing from one place.
Vous me voyez atterrir comme une héroïne?
'Do you see me landing like a heroine?' The little object before 'see' means 'me'. The action after it means landing, and the comparison describes doing so like a female hero.
Ce n'est pas du tout ce que j'avais demandé.

'This is not at all what I had asked for.' The strong negative means 'not at all'. The completed earlier request follows 'what': the director says this is different from what she had asked for. Now let's listen to the entire dialogue once more.
Sofia, on y va?
Oui, je suis prête.
Je m'appelle Sofia Leprince, j'ai 25 ans.
Et mon agent est Gabriel Sarda chez ASK.
Parfait! On commence tout de suite.
D'abord la chorégraphie, ensuite votre scène, d'accord?
D'accord, quand vous voulez.
Ils veulent se battre avec moi?
Je cours plus vite qu'eux!
Maintenant je suis là, maintenant je ne suis plus là!
Vous me voyez atterrir comme une héroïne?
Ce n'est pas du tout ce que j'avais demandé.
Sofia's action performance has avoided the dance the casting director requested. She will now be asked to start over with the choreography. See you next time.
À demain!
